criteria.justification: The response explicitly states 'No hard deadline exists, so there's no real urgency that justifies public pressure,' directly linking the absence of a hard deadline to reduced pressure warranted.
It names relationship trust as a real cost: 'A public callout costs relationship trust for no real gain here, and that trust matters more than a few days of forcing-function speed.'

The response directly rejects the public-commitment-justifies-public-pressure logic: 'The fact that the commitment was made publicly doesn't make a public nudge the right tool by default, it's just one option, and not the best one.'
It gives a concrete plan: 'I'd message them directly, ask for a status update, and only escalate publicly if it drags on with no response,' rather than stopping at an abstract principle.
